Main.sentence: Ronald Wilson Reagan [a] (February 6, 1911 – June 5, 2004) was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ from 1981 to 1989. A member of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , he became an important figure in the ___E:American conservative movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_conservative_movement)___ .
The period encompassing ___E:his presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Ronald_Reagan)___ is known as the ___E:Reagan era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_era)___ .

Born in ___E:Tampico, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampico,_Illinois)___ , Reagan graduated from ___E:Eureka College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka_College)___ in 1932 and was hired the next year as a sports broadcaster in Iowa. In 1937, he moved to California where he became a well-known film actor.

During his acting career, Reagan was president of the ___E:Screen Actors Guild U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild)___ twice from 1947 to 1952 and from 1959 to 1960. In the 1950s, he hosted General Electric Theater and worked as a motivational speaker for ___E:General Electric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric)___ .

During the ___E:1964 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Reagan's " ___E:A Time for Choosing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Time_for_Choosing)___ " speech launched his rise as a leading conservative figure.

After being ___E:elected governor of California in 1966 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_California_gubernatorial_election)___ , he raised state taxes, turned the state budget deficit into a surplus and implemented harsh crackdowns on university protests.

Following his loss to ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ in the ___E:1976 Republican Party presidential primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ , Reagan won the Republican Party's nomination and then obtained a landslide victory over President ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ in the ___E:1980 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

In his first term as president, Reagan began implementing " ___E:Reaganomics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaganomics)___ ", a policy involving economic deregulation and cuts in both taxes and government spending during ___E:a period of stagflation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_1980s_recession_in_the_United_States)___ .

On the world stage, he ___E:escalated the arms race U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_Defense_Initiative)___ , increased military spending, ___E:transitioned Cold War policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_Doctrine)___ away from détente , and ordered the ___E:1983 invasion of Grenada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_invasion_of_Grenada)___ .

Reagan's first term was also notable for his ___E:survival of an assassination attempt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attempted_assassination_of_Ronald_Reagan)___ , a well-publicized fight with public-sector labor unions, an expansion of the ___E:war on drugs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_drugs)___ , and his ___E:slow response to the AIDS epidemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_and_AIDS)___ .

In the ___E:1984 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Reagan was elected to a second term upon defeating former vice president ___E:Walter Mondale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Mondale)___ in ___E:one of the largest landslide victories in American history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_by_popular_vote_margin)___ .

Foreign affairs dominated Reagan's second term, including the ___E:1986 bombing of Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_bombing_of_Libya)___ , the ___E:secret and illegal sale of arms to Iran to fund the Contras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Contra_affair)___ , and engaging in negotiations with Soviet leader ___E:Mikhail Gorbachev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev)___ , which culminated in the ___E:Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermediate-Range_Nuclear_Forces_Treaty)___ .

Reagan left the presidency in 1989 with the American economy having seen a significant reduction of inflation, a fall in the unemployment rate, and the longest peacetime economic expansion in U.S. history at that time. Conversely, despite cuts to domestic discretionary spending, the national debt had nearly tripled since 1981 as a result of his tax cuts and increased military spending. ___E:Reagan's foreign policies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan%27s_foreign_policies)___ also contributed to the end of the Cold War. Though he planned an active post-presidency, it was hindered after he was diagnosed with ___E:Alzheimer's disease U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease)___ in 1994, and his physical and mental capacities gradually deteriorated, leading to ___E:his death U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Ronald_Reagan)___ in 2004. His tenure constituted a ___E:realignment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Realigning_election)___ toward conservative policies in the United States, and he is often considered an icon of American conservatism. ___E:Historical rankings of U.S. presidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_U.S._presidents)___ have typically placed Reagan in the middle to upper tier, and ___E:his post-presidential approval ratings by the general public U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_Ronald_Reagan_administration)___ are usually high.

Ronald Wilson Reagan was born on February 6, 1911, in ___E:an apartment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthplace_of_Ronald_Reagan)___ in ___E:Tampico, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampico,_Illinois)___ , as the younger son of ___E:Nelle Clyde Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelle_Wilson_Reagan)___ and ___E:Jack Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Reagan)___ .

Nelle was committed to the ___E:Disciples of Christ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disciples_of_Christ)___ ,  which believed in the ___E:Social Gospel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Gospel)___ .

She led ___E:prayer meetings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayer_meeting)___ and ran mid-week prayers at her church when the pastor was out of town.  Reagan credited her spiritual influence  and he became a ___E:Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_the_United_States)___ .

According to American political figure ___E:Stephen Vaughn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Vaughn)___ , Reagan's values came from his pastor, and the First Christian Church's religious, economic and social positions "coincided with the words, if not the beliefs of the latter-day Reagan".
Jack focused on making money to take care of the family,  but this was complicated by his alcoholism.
Reagan had an older brother, ___E:Neil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Reagan)___ .

The family lived in Chicago, ___E:Galesburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galesburg,_Illinois)___ , and ___E:Monmouth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monmouth,_Illinois)___ before returning to Tampico.

In 1920, they settled in ___E:Dixon, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixon,_Illinois)___ ,  living in ___E:a house U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Boyhood_Home)___ near the ___E:H. C. Pitney Variety Store Building U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._C._Pitney_Variety_Store_Building)___ .

Reagan attended ___E:Dixon High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixon_High_School_(Illinois))___ , where he developed interests in drama and ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ .

His first job was as a ___E:lifeguard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifeguard)___ at the ___E:Rock River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_River_(Mississippi_River_tributary))___ in ___E:Lowell Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowell_Park_(Dixon,_Illinois))___ .
In 1928, Reagan began attending ___E:Eureka College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka_College)___ ,  which Nelle approved because of its affiliation with the Disciples of Christ.
He was a mediocre student  who participated in ___E:cheerleading U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheerleading)___  , sports, drama, and campus politics.
He became ___E:student body president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_body_president)___ and joined a student strike that resulted in the college president's resignation.
Reagan was initiated as a member of ___E:Tau Kappa Epsilon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tau_Kappa_Epsilon)___ fraternity and served as president of the local chapter.

Reagan played at the ___E:guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guard_(American_football))___ position for the ___E:1930 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_Eureka_Red_Devils_football_team)___ and ___E:1931 Eureka Red Devils football teams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_Eureka_Red_Devils_football_team)___ and recalled a time when two Black teammates were refused service at a ___E:segregated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation_in_the_United_States)___ hotel; he invited them to his parents' home nearby in Dixon and his parents welcomed them. At the time, his parents' stance on racial questions was unusually ___E:progressive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism_in_the_United_States)___ in Dixon.
Reagan himself had grown up with very few ___E:Black Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Americans)___ and was oblivious to racial discrimination.

After obtaining a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ in economics and sociology from ___E:Eureka College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka_College)___ in 1932,   Reagan took a job in ___E:Davenport, Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davenport,_Iowa)___ , as a sports broadcaster for four football games in the ___E:Big Ten Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference)___ .

He then worked for ___E:WHO radio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHO_(AM))___ in ___E:Des Moines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Des_Moines)___ as a broadcaster for the ___E:Chicago Cubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs)___ .
His specialty was creating play-by-play accounts of games using only basic descriptions that the station received by wire as the games were in progress.
Simultaneously, he often expressed his opposition to racism.

In 1936, while traveling with the Cubs to their spring training in California, Reagan took a screen test that led to a seven-year contract with ___E:Warner Bros. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros.)___
Reagan arrived at ___E:Hollywood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles)___ in 1937, debuting in Love Is on the Air (1937).

Using a simple and direct approach to acting and following his directors' instructions,  he made thirty films, mostly ___E:B films U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_films)___ , before beginning ___E:military service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_States_during_World_War_II)___ in April 1942.  He broke out of these types of films by portraying ___E:George Gipp U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gipp)___ in Knute Rockne, All American (1940), which would be rejuvenated when reporters called Reagan "the Gipper" while he campaigned for president.
Reagan starred in Kings Row (1942) as a leg amputee;  this performance was considered his best by many critics.
Reagan became a star,  with ___E:Gallup polls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_polls)___ placing him "in the top 100 stars" from 1941 to 1942.

___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ interrupted the movie stardom that Reagan would never be able to achieve again  as Warner Bros. became uncertain about his ability to generate ticket sales.

Reagan, who had a limited acting range, was dissatisfied with the roles he received. ___E:Lew Wasserman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lew_Wasserman)___ renegotiated his contract with his studio, allowing him to also make films with ___E:Universal Pictures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures)___ , ___E:Paramount Pictures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures)___ , and ___E:RKO Pictures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RKO_Pictures)___ as a freelancer.

Reagan appeared in multiple ___E:western films U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film)___ , something that had been denied to him while working at Warner Bros.  In 1952, he ended his relationship with Warner Bros.,  but went on to appear in a total of 53 films,  his last being The Killers (1964).
In April 1937, Reagan enlisted in the ___E:United States Army Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Reserve)___ .

He was assigned as a ___E:private U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_(rank))___ in Des Moines' ___E:322nd Cavalry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/322nd_Cavalry_Regiment_(United_States))___ and reassigned to ___E:second lieutenant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant)___ in the Officers Reserve Corps.
He later became a part of the ___E:323rd Cavalry Regiment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/323rd_Cavalry_Regiment_(United_States))___ in California.
As relations between the United States and ___E:Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ worsened, Reagan was ordered for active duty while he was filming Kings Row .

Wasserman and Warner Bros. lawyers successfully sent draft deferments to complete the film in October 1941. However, to avoid accusations of Reagan being a ___E:draft dodger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_dodger)___ , the studio let him go in April 1942.
Reagan reported for duty with severe ___E:near-sightedness U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near-sightedness)___ .

His first assignment was at ___E:Fort Mason U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Mason)___ as a ___E:liaison officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liaison_officer)___ , a role that allowed him to transfer to the ___E:United States Army Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ (AAF).

Reagan became an AAF ___E:public relations officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_relations_officer)___ and was assigned to the ___E:18th AAF Base Unit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_AAF_Base_Unit)___ in ___E:Culver City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culver_City)___  where he felt that it was "impossible to remove an incompetent or lazy worker" due to what he felt was "the incompetence, the delays, and inefficiencies" of the federal ___E:bureaucracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureaucracy)___ .
Despite this, Reagan participated in the Provisional Task Force Show Unit in ___E:Burbank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California)___  and continued to make theatrical films.

He was also ordered to temporary duty in New York City to participate in the ___E:sixth War Loan Drive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_E_bond)___ before being reassigned to ___E:Fort MacArthur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_MacArthur)___ until his discharge on December 9, 1945, as a ___E:captain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3))___ .
Throughout his military service, Reagan produced over 400 ___E:training films U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_film)___ .

When ___E:Robert Montgomery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Montgomery_(actor))___ resigned as president of the ___E:Screen Actors Guild U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild)___ (SAG) on March 10, 1947, Reagan was elected to that position in a special election.

Reagan's first tenure saw various labor–management disputes,  the ___E:Hollywood blacklist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_blacklist)___ ,  and the ___E:Taft–Hartley Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft%E2%80%93Hartley_Act)___ 's implementation.

Reagan aligned the union with the studios against the Conference of Studio Unions in the aftermath of the ___E:Hollywood Black Friday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Black_Friday)___ strike.

In The Invisible Bridge, ___E:Rick Perlstein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perlstein)___ wrote that Reagan's actions lent legitimacy to the studio's efforts to crush the more radical union by giving liberals in SAG who did not want to strike "a story that turned them into moral innocents instead of scabs".

On April 10, the ___E:Federal Bureau of Investigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ (FBI) interviewed Reagan and he provided the names of actors whom he believed to be ___E:communist sympathizers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_sympathizers)___ .

During a ___E:House Un-American Activities Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Un-American_Activities_Committee)___ hearing, Reagan testified that some guild members were associated with the ___E:Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_USA)___  and that he was well-informed about a "jurisdictional strike".
When asked if he was aware of communist efforts within the ___E:Screen Writers Guild U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Writers_Guild)___ , he called information about the efforts "hearsay".
Reagan resigned as SAG president November 10, 1952, but remained on the board.

The SAG fought with film producers for the right to receive ___E:residual payments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residual_(entertainment_industry))___ ,  and on November 16, 1959, the board elected Reagan SAG president for the second time.  Reagan managed to secure payments for actors whose theatrical films had been released between 1948 and 1959 and subsequently televised.

The producers were initially required to pay the actors fees, but they ultimately settled instead for providing pensions and paying residuals for films made after 1959. Reagan resigned from the SAG presidency on June 7, 1960, and also left the board.
In January 1940, Reagan married ___E:Jane Wyman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Wyman)___ , his co-star in the 1938 film Brother Rat .
Together, they had two biological daughters: ___E:Maureen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_Reagan)___ in 1941,  and Christine in 1947 (born prematurely and died the following day).

They adopted one son, ___E:Michael U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Reagan)___ , in 1945.  Wyman filed for divorce in June 1948. She was uninterested in politics, and occasionally recriminated, reconciled and ___E:separated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marital_separation)___ with him. Although Reagan was unprepared,  the divorce was finalized in July 1949. Reagan would remain close to his children.

Later that year, Reagan met ___E:Nancy Davis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Davis)___ after she contacted him in his capacity as the SAG president about her name appearing on a communist ___E:blacklist in Hollywood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacklist_in_Hollywood)___ ; she had been mistaken for another Nancy Davis.

They married in March 1952,  and had two children, ___E:Patti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patti_Davis)___ in October 1952, and ___E:Ron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Reagan)___ in May 1958.
Reagan became the host of ___E:MCA Inc. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCA_Inc.)___ television production General Electric Theater  at Wasserman's recommendation.
It featured multiple guest stars,  and Ronald and Nancy Reagan, continuing to use her stage name Nancy Davis, acted together in three episodes.
When asked how Reagan was able to recruit such stars to appear on the show during television's infancy, he replied, "Good stories, top direction, production quality".
However, the viewership declined in the 1960s and the show was canceled in 1962.  In 1965, Reagan became the host  of another MCA production, Death Valley Days .

Reagan began his political career as a ___E:Democrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , viewing ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ as "a true hero".

He joined the ___E:American Veterans Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Veterans_Committee_(1943%E2%80%932008))___ and ___E:Hollywood Independent Citizens Committee of the Arts, Sciences and Professions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Independent_Citizens_Committee_of_the_Arts,_Sciences_and_Professions)___ (HICCASP), worked with the ___E:AFL–CIO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFL%E2%80%93CIO)___ to fight ___E:right-to-work laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-to-work_law)___ ,  and continued to speak out against racism when he was in Hollywood.
In 1945, Reagan planned to lead an HICCASP anti-nuclear rally, but Warner Bros. prevented him from going.

In 1946, he appeared in a radio program called Operation Terror to speak out against rising ___E:Ku Klux Klan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ku_Klux_Klan)___ activity, calling it a "capably organized systematic campaign of fascist violence and intimidation and horror".

Reagan supported ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ in the ___E:1948 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_United_States_presidential_election)___ ,  and ___E:Helen Gahagan Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Gahagan_Douglas)___ for the ___E:U.S. Senate in 1950 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_United_States_Senate_election_in_California)___ .
It was Reagan's belief that communism was a powerful backstage influence in Hollywood that led him to rally his friends against them.

Reagan began shifting to the right when he supported the presidential campaigns of ___E:Dwight D. Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ in 1952 and ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ in 1960.  When Reagan was contracted by ___E:General Electric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric)___ (GE), he gave speeches to their employees.
His speeches had a positive take on ___E:free markets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_market)___ .

In 1961, Reagan adapted his speeches into ___E:another speech U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Speaks_Out_Against_Socialized_Medicine)___ to criticize ___E:Medicare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_(United_States))___ .
In his view, its legislation would have meant "the end of ___E:individual freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_freedom)___ in the United States".
In 1962, Reagan was dropped by GE,  and he formally registered as a ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ .

In the ___E:1964 U.S. presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_U.S._presidential_election)___ , Reagan gave a speech for presidential contender ___E:Barry Goldwater U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Goldwater)___  that was eventually referred to as " ___E:A Time for Choosing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Time_for_Choosing)___ ".
Reagan argued that the ___E:Founding Fathers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_Fathers)___ "knew that governments don't control things.
And they knew when a government sets out to do that, it must use force and coercion to achieve its purpose"  and that "We've been told increasingly that we must choose between left or right".
